name: MinimalForwarder unguarded execute on BSC
summary: KiloEx's BSC MinimalForwarder exposes a public execute((address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes),bytes) entry point that relays any request with a valid signature but omits the keeper and approved-router authorization enforced by its other relay entry point. Because the request chooses its own signer and the downstream delegate trusts msg.sender == the forwarder without checking the appended ERC-2771 sender, the attacker used a self-generated signer to reach the privileged price-and-trade path, set artificial prices, and trade against KiloEx's USDT vault.
notes: The second and final pre-exploit Upgraded event from the forwarder proxy selected implementation 0xd8240094e57bf5f893420ffc1e750c94de4a4177. The EIP-1967 implementation slot changes from 0xde6f7616d7a18831445ca064a0351c4b603aad2b at block 47331738 to 0xd8240094e57bf5f893420ffc1e750c94de4a4177 at block 47331739 and still holds the latter address immediately before the exploit.

Three calls using the unguarded forwarder entry point define the BSC campaign. In the first two, KiloEx USDT vault 0xef7af0804aab3885da59a8236fabfa19ddc6cf48 loses a transaction-local net 892947.452212280000000000 and 61974.379910380000000000 USDT. In the third, the attacker directly relays USDT.transfer through the forwarder and removes 4306.800000000000000000 USDT of accumulated KiloEx fees. The resulting gross KiloEx outflow is 959228.632122660000000000 USDT; the attacker EOA receives 959217.079253360000000000 USDT, with the difference going to flash-loan and protocol fees. This record covers BSC only and does not include the separately recorded Base loss or the out-of-scope opBNB leg. Later recovery under the cross-chain bounty agreement is not netted out of the exploit-time gross loss. Base leg of the same campaign (USDC component): Three exploit transactions (blocks 28933730, 28933848, 28935593) net 3,323,209.390248 USDC out of the KiloEx USDC liquidity pool 0xdf5acc616cd3ea9556ec340a11b54859a393ebbb, whose USDC balance falls from 3,323,951.604434 at block 28933729 to 1,555.175358 at block 28935593 (the residual difference is unrelated third-party deposits between the exploit transactions). Of that outflow the attacker EOA 0x00fac92881556a90fdb19eae9f23640b95b4bcbd keeps 3,323,170.888033 USDC; 15 USDC is the Uniswap V3 flash-loan fee and 23.502215 USDC is a KiloEx vault fee. This record covers the Base leg only; the BSC leg is a separate record and opBNB is out of the corpus, so the widely reported ~7.5M campaign figure is not used here. Between 2025-04-15 and 2025-04-18 the attacker returned the proceeds under a 10% bounty deal (on Base: 305.536342416848900260 ETH, 10,551.589691 USDC, 232.193079 USDT and 0.090531 USDbC to 0xd38a22f5330f45162f13086d6ccbde0335c1ae9e). Recovery is not netted out of the exploit-time gross figure.

The same attacker exercised the byte-identical Base deployment of MinimalForwarder (0x3274b668aed85479e2a8511e74d7db7240ebe7c8) one minute later, starting with 0x6b378c84aa57097fb5845f285476e33d6832b8090d36d02fe0e1aed909228edd. That leg is merged here as the 3323209.390248 USDC component; the code age is measured on the BSC anchor.
